title: mut.feedback
mutation_directive: BREAK THE FORM — the current attractor+glyph execution is conceptually right but visually expected. Pick ONE of these unexpected structural moves and commit to it fully: (A) DUAL-ATTRACTOR CIVIL WAR — at t≈20s, a second attractor (Thomas symmetric or Halvorsen) phase-locks with the Aizawa; particles are caught between two gravitational bodies, forming visible bifurcation threads and contested zones where glyphs flicker between two alphabets (Latin vs CJK / Arabic); the two attractors slowly drift apart then re-merge — metaphor: language vs code fighting for the same minds. Implement as two GPGPU ping-pong textures blended by a per-particle ownership scalar. (B) CURSOR WRITES THE POEM — pointer doesn't nudge parameters, it ABSORBS nearby glyphs (within 0.3 world units); detached glyphs trail the cursor in a fluid arc of magnetic ink; on pointer-stop they snap back to nearest attractor surface and reassemble into a new word drawn from a small embedded vocabulary. Your movement through the field IS the poem. No UI, no instructions — discovery through touch. (C) SEMIOTIC COLLAPSE + REBIRTH — over 90 seconds, glyphs continuously evolve: Latin → Arabic → Devanagari → CJK → geometric primitives (△ ○ □) → pure noise pixels → back to Latin. Each alphabet uses its own atlas texture; a LERP scalar drives the crossfade in the GPGPU shader. The full arc is one 'translation.' Whichever direction chosen: must feel like something a viewer has NEVER SEEN before in browser-native three.js. Ship ONE idea executed at 100%, not three at 30%.

threejs_review.directive: Replace CPU attractor integration with webgl_gpgpu_protoplanet-style GPUComputationRenderer to support 160×160=25600 particles with multi-attractor blending and per-particle atlas-lerp in a single compute pass, unlocking fluid semiotic transitions at full density.
